messages:
Priya (sales): FYI—ACME wants to run a POC using a community model they trained called zephyr-34b-v2. They asked whether Redwood can serve it (hosting + dedicated) and what the onboarding timeline looks like.
Kevin (solutions): Good catch. Do we know: model format (hf/ggml/torch), tokenizer, max seq length, and whether they need KV cache persistence?
Priya (sales): They sent a short spec: PyTorch state_dict + tokenizer JSON. Max seq length 8192. They specifically called out ~100 concurrent users peak, avg request ~600 tokens.
Anya (product): Catalog-side notes: we support custom model onboarding but need a verification run (compat test + perf profile). For new 34B variants we typically generate three "profiles": hosted-optimized, ded-quantized, private-raw. Can we validate quantization compatibility?
Oliver (eng-ml): Quick checklist from runtime POV:
- Confirm architecture (transformer LM, causal) -> OK?
- Model sharded or single-file?
- Parameter layout (KV cache format) -> influences kernel selection
- FP16/FP32 weights to decide quant flow
If they provide fp32/state_dict we can attempt 4-bit quantization (q4_0/q4_K) but need to run accuracy regressions.
Kevin (solutions): For the POC timeline: if artifacts are ready we can do a smoke compatibility run in our staging within 3 business days. Full perf profiling (latency/cost) on hosted takes ~7 business days including automated evals. Dedicated onboarding (reserved) add ~2 weeks for capacity planning + SLA paperwork.
Priya (sales): They also asked about pricing — is there a quick estimate for tokens vs reserved? They expect 100 concurrent, 600 tokens avg, 100k requests/day.
Anya (product): Back-of-envelope hosted tokens cost = tokens * per-token rate. For zephyr-34b-v2 we'll likely map it to our 34B performance curve; hosted per-token will be higher than 7B but lower than 70B. For Dedicated, we should model using expected throughput: 100 concurrent * 600 tokens ≈ 60k tokens/sec peak? Wait math check.
Kevin (solutions): Clarify: 100 concurrent * 600 tokens per request across the whole request lifespan. If concurrency sustained and latency ~1.5s, throughput ≈ (100 * 600)/1.5 ≈ 40k tokens/s peak. We'll need to size GPUs accordingly (2x A100-80GB or 4x H100s depending on quant). I'll prepare a sizing doc.
Jade (security): On questionnaire for enterprise: licensing for zephyr-34b-v2 (OSS license type), provenance of training data, artifact signing, and dependency SCA. Also need to know whether model includes any private PII or proprietary corpora. We must collect: model license file, training data summary, and an ISO/ SOC checklist for Private deployments.
Priya (sales): Customer says license is an "MIT-like" permissive variant but they will confirm. They said training data is internal + some web crawl; they need to check PII exposure.
Oliver (eng-ml): Actionable next steps from eng side: ask customer for a small test artifact (first 100M params subset or a minimal example with tokenizer + model config) so we can run a dry-load and tokenization checks. Also request a sample prompt set for quality regression.
Kevin (solutions): I'll share the onboarding playbook link and an upload endpoint for artifacts. Use this curl to PUT:
```
curl -X POST https://upload.redwood.ai/models -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -F "model=@zephyr-34b-v2.pth" -F "tokenizer=@tokenizer.json" -F "metadata=@metadata.json"
```
Priya (sales): Can we commit to the 3-business-day smoke run? Customer wants that for their internal demo.
Oliver (eng-ml): Yes if artifacts arrive by EOD tomorrow we can queue the smoke compatibility job. We need the full state_dict + tokenizer + example inputs.
Anya (product): I'll reserve a model slot in the staging catalog and predefine two candidate variants: zephyr-34b-v2 (fp16 hosted) and zephyr-34b-v2-q4 (quantized). We'll tag expected perf bands.
Jade (security): I'll start the security questionnaire template and add model-specific sections (license, training data, threat model). Will need security contact at ACME for SSO/KMS details if they go Dedicated/Private.
Kevin (solutions): Regarding compatibility checks: we'll run these automated tests: model-load, forward pass (1 token and long-seq), KV cache correctness, batch/streaming behavior, and inference determinism check. Any failing test -> list of mitigations (repackaging, patching attention kernel).
Priya (sales): ACME reps want a note on how we handle fallbacks if the model is too slow in hosted — can we do an automatic fallback to a smaller variant?
Anya (product): Yes, smart routing supports fallback policies. We can configure their route to prefer zephyr-34b-v2 and fallback to zephyr-7b-v1 if latency breaches SLO. We'll need both variants in catalog and a routing policy.
Kevin (solutions): I'll draft an email to ACME with: artifact upload link, required files checklist, expected timeline (smoke 3 days, perf 7 days, dedicated onboarding +2w), and preliminary sizing estimate.
Priya (sales): Perfect. Assigning owners: Kevin = POC tech lead, Oliver = runtime validation, Anya = catalog/profile + pricing estimate, Jade = security questionnaire.
DeployBot: New upload endpoint created: https://upload.redwood.ai/models (expires in 72h) :white_check_mark:
Priya (sales): I'll send the intro now and copy the team. Thanks all :pray:
